name: Swiss Chard
family: Amaranthaceae, the amaranth and goosefoot family
grown_as: Leaf beet grown for its big leaves and thick coloured stalks, picked from the outside over a long season. William's records list 'Rainbow Mix': stalks red, pink, orange, yellow or white from plant to plant. Drawn with a mix of stalk colours. ⚠️ CHECK the colours wanted.
habit: A big upright rosette 40 to 60 cm tall and 30 to 45 cm across, from a thick crown on a tough taproot (not swollen like beetroot). A biennial: in the second year a leafy, branched flowering stem 1 to 1.5 m.

leaf.outline: Large, oval to oblong, 20 to 30 cm long
leaf.base: Rounded to slightly heart-shaped, the blade running a little way down each side of the stalk
leaf.margin: Smooth, no teeth, wavy and often curled
leaf.veins: A very broad, flat, fleshy midrib 2 to 5 cm wide carrying on straight from the stalk, in the stalk colour; side veins branching from it, often tinted the same colour
leaf.surface: Glossy and hairless, strongly puckered and blistered between the veins
leaf.stalk: Thick, fleshy, flattened and crisp, 15 to 30 cm, as wide as a finger or more, glossy red, pink, orange, yellow or white
leaf.colour: Dark glossy green, or bronze-green over red stalks

flower.form: Tiny green star-shaped flowers without petals, in clusters along long thin spikes
flower.petals: None: five small green tepals, curved inwards
flower.centre: Five short stamens with yellow anthers round a low green centre
flower.behind: A small narrow green bract under each cluster
flower.carried: Stalkless in clusters of two or three, spaced along long, slender, leafy spikes that branch from a tall stem; the spikes arch and droop at the tips
flower.season: June to August of the second year

fruit: The flowers in each cluster fuse as they ripen into a hard, corky, knobbly 'seed' (a seed ball) 3 to 5 mm across, light brown, holding two to four true seeds. One seed ball sown gives a clump of seedlings.
seedling: Seedlings come up in little clumps from each seed ball. Two narrow strap-shaped glossy seed leaves on a stem already coloured red, yellow or white, then oval true leaves on coloured stalks.
winter: Often survives a mild winter as a smaller rosette of reddened leaves, growing again in spring before it flowers.

leaf: a large glossy, strongly puckered blade with smooth wavy edges
a very broad flat coloured midrib running on from the stalk
bloom: tiny green flowers with no petals
stalkless in small clusters along a thin spike
seed: a knobbly corky brown seed ball 3 to 5 mm
several seeds in one, so one sown gives a clump
seedling: a coloured stem (red, yellow or white)
young: an upright rosette of glossy puckered leaves
crop: a big upright rosette of large dark puckered leaves
thick stalks in several colours (red, yellow, white)
flower: a tall leafy stem branching into long thin arching spikes
seedhead: long spikes crowded with brown knobbly seed balls

look_alikes: Spinach beet has thin green stalks and smaller, smoother leaves. Rhubarb has red stalks but huge, rough, ragged-edged leaves and is poisonous in leaf. Beetroot leaves are smaller, on a swollen root.
